newsitem.title: USA: Phoenix Gold sees lower Q3 revs, profit.
newsitem.headline: Phoenix Gold sees lower Q3 revs, profit.

text.p: Phoenix Gold International Inc said late Monday that it expects its third quarter revenue and net profit to come in below analysts' expectations.

The company attributed the lower-than-expected revenue in the third quarter primarily to production issues related to certain car audio amplifiers and car audio speakers. The company said it also recently experienced some softness in demand in the professional audio amplifier market.

Analysts' mean estimate for earnings per share in the third quarter is $0.24, according to First Call. Analysts' expectations for revenue in that period was not available, and Phoenix Gold did not immediately return a telephone call.

"We are of course disappointed that production problems will cause sales revenue not to meet expectations, but we are encouraged with our progress towards profitability," Chief Operating Officer Timothy Johnson said in a statement.
Phoenix Gold designs, markets and sells electronics, accessories and speakers.
In the prior year's third quarter, the company reported net income of $185,384, or $0.05 per share, on sales of $7.46 million.
